A second investigator, starting fresh with the same tools, tested the kind of each fault in your draft answer. Their findings:

### `ts-seat-service`: you said `network_delay`. They conclude `network_loss` (confidence: medium).
Scope: Affected: the ts-seat-service to ts-config-service connection, specifically its GET /api/v1/configservice/configs/{configName} calls. About 17% of those calls carry an extra 180 to 240 ms, with a tail reaching several seconds, while the median stays at normal. Through the seat service's left_tickets endpoint this tail reaches travel, travel-plan and travel2 as a p95 rise to about 420 to 840 ms. Not affected: the callee's own processing (config's Server span stays about 2 ms), seat's other outgoing connections (order, order-other, about 1.2 ms gap), inbound gaps to seat (about 1.1 ms), and every call's error share, which is 0. Network_partition and network_corrupt cannot be separated from network_loss on these signals; the chosen kind belongs to the loss/partition class and corruption is not excluded.
Ruled out:
- `network_delay`: The median and quartiles on the seat-to-config connection are flat: p25 0.06 ms, p50 0.09 ms, against a normal gap of about 0.14 ms. Delay would shift every call. Only the p90 and p95 move (216 and 422 ms), and about 82 of 489 calls sit in the 180 to 240 ms band, which is the TCP retransmission-timeout step signature of loss, not delay.
- `http_aborted`: Error share is 0.00 on every edge the claim touches, and no call fails. The slow calls complete normally, so there is no application-level cut.
- `dns_lookup_failed`: Calls complete with no failures and the slow ones are a tail of completed calls, not name-resolution failures. No DNS error signal appears in the data queried.

- `database_call_slow`: The affected calls are HTTP GETs to config with no traced database child. The gap appears on the wire between the two spans, not in a DB call inside either service.

About 17% of those calls carry an extra 180 to 240 ms, with a tail reaching several seconds, while the median stays at normal. Through the seat service's left_tickets endpoint this tail reaches travel, travel-plan and travel2 as a p95 rise to about 420 to 840 ms. Not affected: the callee's own processing (config's Server span stays about 2 ms), seat's other outgoing connections (order, order-other, about 1.2 ms gap), inbound gaps to seat (about 1.1 ms), and every call's error share, which is 0. Network_partition and network_corrupt cannot be separated from network_loss on these signals; the chosen kind belongs to the loss/partition class and corruption is not excluded.

ruled_out.why: The median and quartiles on the seat-to-config connection are flat: p25 0.06 ms, p50 0.09 ms, against a normal gap of about 0.14 ms. Delay would shift every call. Only the p90 and p95 move (216 and 422 ms), and about 82 of 489 calls sit in the 180 to 240 ms band, which is the TCP retransmission-timeout step signature of loss, not delay.
Error share is 0.00 on every edge the claim touches, and no call fails. The slow calls complete normally, so there is no application-level cut.
Calls complete with no failures and the slow ones are a tail of completed calls, not name-resolution failures. No DNS error signal appears in the data queried.

The callee config service stays alive: its spans per minute go 515 to 666 and metric rows 67 to 191 in the incident. The seat service also keeps emitting spans (409 to 455 per minute). Calls are not refused or silent.

The slow time sits in the Client GET span, not inside any process. Config's Server span stays at about 2 ms p50, and seat's own left_tickets Server self-time p95 is about 1 ms, so no method inside the process has grown.
The affected calls are HTTP GETs to config with no traced database child. The gap appears on the wire between the two spans, not in a DB call inside either service.

**Verdict: the evidence does not support `network_delay`. It points to a tail-only transport fault on the ts-seat-service → ts-config-service connection, most consistent with `network_loss` (or `network_corrupt`, which the telemetry cannot separate from it). Confidence: moderate-high against delay, moderate for the loss family.**

**What the data shows**

I pulled the per-call gap (Client span minus Server span) for every call touching ts-seat-service in the abnormal period:

| Connection | n | gap p25 | gap p50 | gap p90 | gap p95 | calls in 180–240 ms | calls > 1 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| seat → config, GET configs | 489 | 0.06 | 0.09 | 216 | 422 | 82 | 8 |
| seat → order-other, POST | 173 | 1.19 | 1.22 | 1.31 | 1.32 | 0 | 0 |
| seat → order, POST | 168 | 1.16 | 1.18 | 1.25 | 1.28 | 0 | 0 |
| travel → seat, left_tickets | 153 | 1.09 | 1.11 | 1.17 | 1.19 | 0 | 0 |
| travel-plan → seat, left_tickets | 101 | 1.10 | 1.14 | 1.19 | 1.21 | 0 | 0 |
| travel2 → seat, left_tickets | 87 | 1.12 | 1.15 | 1.23 | 1.25 | 0 | 0 |
| preserve → seat, POST | 17 | 1.25 | 1.27 | 1.30 | 1.30 | 0 | 0 |

1. **Delay is ruled out by the shape.** Network delay moves every call by about the same amount, so the 25th and 50th percentiles would rise with the 95th. Here the p25 (0.06 ms) and p50 (0.09 ms) are essentially unchanged from normal (the lead's normal gap was 0.14 ms). Only the tail moves.
2. **The tail has the loss/corruption signature.** About 17% of the seat→config calls sit in the 180–240 ms band, which matches TCP's retransmission timeout (~200 ms), and the rest of the tail spreads out to multi-second values. That is the step pattern the boundary rules describe for loss or corruption.
3. **Nothing fails.** Error share is 0.00 on every edge, and config's own Server span stays at about 2 ms. Calls get through, just occasionally after a retransmit. That argues against partition (which would fail calls or hang them to a timeout) and against an application fault (the time is on the wire, not in config).
4. **The fault is confined to one connection.** Seat's other outgoing connections (order, order-other) and all inbound connections to seat show gaps of about 1.2 ms, unchanged. The slowdown is not a general seat-pod problem.
5. **The 420 ms seen by callers is inherited.** Travel, travel-plan and travel2 see a Client p95 of about 420–840 ms on left_tickets, but their gap to seat is still about 1.1 ms. Seat's own Server time is about 1 ms at p95 (the Client GET child carries the ~420 ms). The callers' slowdown is the seat→config tail propagating up, so the survey's "own p95 206 ms" for seat should not be read as seat's own processing.

**Limits**

- Loss and corruption produce the same signature here, so I cannot say which one it is. The equivalence-class rule covers loss vs partition, but corruption would be a separate answer. Nothing in the traces (no deserialization errors, no checksum errors in logs) pointed me to corruption.
- I did not check seat's container metrics or config's logs in detail, so I have not ruled out a process-level cause on the seat side. The per-call gap, though, is the wire-level evidence.
- The fault is on the seat→config connection, which is the scope the claim names. I have not tested whether ts-seat-service is the right service to blame.
